mechanism_implication: Pre-equilibrium argmax saturation is mechanism-locked at three levels: (K15f) NOT gating-driven — saturation forms within 1-2 LoRA updates after activation regardless of gate window; (K15m) NOT magnitude-driven — linear LR warmup over first {10, 20, 50} steps does not prevent saturation; (K15n) NOT initial-condition-driven — perturbing LoRA-B from N(0, sigma^2) with sigma in {0.001, 0.01, 0.1} does not prevent saturation. Combined: saturation is DIRECTION-driven, not magnitude- or initial-condition-driven. The pretrained DLM's confident argmax distribution dominates the first 1-2 LoRA forward+backward updates regardless of LoRA init, LR schedule, or activation window. This is the 8th disclosed-negative intervention in the paper and the strongest evidence yet that the pre-equilibrium mechanism is STRUCTURAL to LoRA-on-DLM at the tested 200-step PEFT horizon, not modifiable by single-axis interventions on LoRA init, magnitude, or gating.
prior_art_note: Standard LoRA (Hu et al. 2021) initializes A Kaiming-uniform and B zero so BA=0 at step 0 (identity behavior). DoRA, AdaLoRA, rsLoRA also preserve B=0 at init. No prior published work tests nonzero LoRA-B init for DLM PEFT instability specifically. K15n fills this gap and confirms the zero-LoRA-B init is NOT a contributing factor to the saturation mechanism.
schema: K15n adapter-init perturbation: LoRA-B initialized from N(0, sigma^2) instead of zero. Tests whether breaking the zero-init breaks rapid-post-update saturation. MDLM-OWT 130M, r in {4,16,64} x rho in {0.05,0.40,0.90} x n=3 seeds x sigma in {0.001, 0.01, 0.1} = 81 cells.
verdict: NEGATIVE — fire rate 27/27 across all sigma values (0.001, 0.01, 0.1) identical to K15a baseline (sigma=0). Fire-step median 11 unchanged. Saturation is NOT initial-condition-locked. Adapter-init perturbation does NOT prevent rapid-post-update top-1 saturation.
